title: Restriction-form transition of simultaneous derived direct image
statement:
Let $u:V\to W$ be any morphism of schemes, and use small representatives of their pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any strict tower of sheaves of commutative rings on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $C_n=u^{-1}B_n$, and use the induced tower on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $\mathscr S(B),\mathscr S(C)$ be the strict semilinear module-system categories, with their ordinary unbounded derived categories and the simultaneous direct image $G=Ru_{*,\bullet}$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $G_n=Ru_{*,B_n}$, and for $m\ge n$ write $r^W_{m,n},r^V_{m,n}$ for exact restriction of scalars along $B_m\to B_n,C_m\to C_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\delta_{m,n}:G_m r^V_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}r^W_{m,n}G_n$ be the inverse of the canonical ring-sheaf-change comparison $d$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. For $N\in D(\mathscr S(C))$, let $a^N_{m,n}:N_m\to r^V_{m,n}N_n$ and $a^{GN}_{m,n}:(GN)_m\to r^W_{m,n}(GN)_n$ be its actual derived restriction-form transitions. Under the canonical natural evaluation isomorphisms $e_nG\cong G_ne_n$, one has
$$a^{GN}_{m,n}=\delta_{m,n,N_n}\circ G_m(a^N_{m,n}).$$
The formula is natural in $N$ and includes $m=n$. Its comparison has this normalization: for a K-injective $C_n$-complex $I$ and a K-injective replacement $r^V_{m,n}I\to H$ over $C_m$, $\delta_{m,n,QI}$ is the inverse of the class of $u_*r^V_{m,n}I=r^W_{m,n}u_*I\to u_*H$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. No flatness of the tower maps, normalization of $N$, or preservation of K-injectives by restriction or evaluation is assumed. Write $T=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$ and $S=-\otimes^L_{C_m}C_n$, with their exact restriction-of-scalars right adjoints [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $b:TG_m\to G_nS$ be the coefficient-extension mate specified in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For every $M\in D(C_m)$, $L\in D(C_n)$ and $a:M\to r^V_{m,n}L$, the same comparison satisfies the scalar-transpose identity
$$\bigl(\delta_{m,n,L}\circ G_m(a)\bigr)^\sharp=G_n(a^\sharp)\circ b_M.$$
Here sharp denotes precisely the two coefficient extension/restriction adjunction bijections. Thus the scalar mate of the resolution-normalized restriction comparison is the specified system coefficient mate.

proof.text: Prove the localization calculation for abstract exact functors first, then specialize to the ordinary horizontal transition square ordinaryPullTransition degreewise. Reuse the proved exactSquare_fac normalization of the exact-square composition module. For Q of a complex, postcompose with the three invertible exact-functor factors. Naturality of the restriction and evaluation comparisons, together with the defining liftNatTrans factorization of derivedTransition, reduces the equation to Q of the ordinary square. Localization.natTrans_ext extends it to every derived system. Transpose this localized pull square using the two evaluated counit equations. The coefficient mate counit equation and naturality of the system counit give the restriction-form push-transition equation after cancelling delta.inv.

proof.text: The ordinary direct-image mate is invertible. Apply the underlying set-sheaf functor to the ordinary module Hom correspondence. The normalized level unit makes it the original topos Hom correspondence. restrictionPullback_underlying identifies the two underlying left-adjoint arrows, so the underlying mate followed by levelPushUnderlying is exactly the other levelPushUnderlying. Hence its underlying map is an isomorphism; the forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0D6D and 0D6E, normalized coefficient-square calculation; Zheng Construction 4.1 for ordinary horizontal transitions.

proof.text: Apply the proved derived_mate_factors calculation of the ring-change module to the ordinary restrictionPullback square and the two canonical level adjunctions. On a K-injective I, its right-derived unit is the inverse of rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. Postcompose the comparison equation with right-derived image of Q(j), use naturality of the right-derived unit, and cancel the invertible comparison on I. This gives exactly the displayed resolution equation for every j into a K-injective H. For a quasi-isomorphism j, its left side is invertible, since delta.inv and the exact restriction factors are invertible. All factors on the right except Q(u_*j) are invertible by the preceding step, so Q(u_*j) is invertible. The localization criterion for quasi-isomorphisms proves the required acyclicity. This avoids a separate derived-composition theorem and makes no preservation-of-K-injectives claim.
